# nbskill


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`nbskill` is a Python Pyskill for agents and maintainers working on nbdev notebooks. It keeps stable cell identities, chapter context, execution evidence, and source diffs together. The notebooks teach the same workflow that the installed functions implement.

``` python
from pyskills import doc, list_pyskills
from nbskill import skill
from nbskill.foundation import cell_source, parse_cells
from nbskill.graph import notebook_knowledge_graph_data
from nbskill.read import context
```

## Why it exists

A notebook contains more than Python source. Explanations, examples, outputs, and cell metadata matter when changing a library. `nbskill` selects chapters and symbols before editing and validates a batch before writing it. A failed edit leaves the file unchanged; successful edits retain the source cell IDs and produce reviewable diffs.

`nbformat` handles notebook data, `execnb` executes cells, and nbdev exports and publishes the library. `nbskill` combines those tasks for an agent that must choose a small scope, make a structured change, and check its evidence. Use it when these notebook boundaries matter.

## Choose a tool

| Need | Public operation |
|----|----|
| Find the relevant chapter or symbol | [`context`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/read.html#context) |
| Route generated Python back to its source notebook | [`generated_owner`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/foundation.html#generated_owner) |

| Review changed cell source and notebook style | [`diff_nb`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/review.html#diff_nb), [`style_check`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/review.html#style_check) |
| Assess execution evidence after a change | [`notebook_state`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/state.html#notebook_state) |
| Search prior implementations before adding a helper | [`reference_query`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/knowledge.html#reference_query) |

Load `nbskill.skill` through Pyskills, then read `doc()` for the callable you intend to use. Its signature and parameter documentation are the operation’s contract.

## Parse notebook cells

[`parse_cells`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/foundation.html#parse_cells) accepts a compact text format with `%%markdown`, `%%code`, and `---` boundaries. This is useful when proposing several cells without notebook JSON. The result retains the two different cell types:

``` python
cell_text = "\n".join(["%%markdown", "## Demo", "---", "%%code", "value = 42"])
parsed_cells = parse_cells(cell_text)
assert [cell.cell_type for cell in parsed_cells] == ["markdown", "code"]
[(cell.cell_type, cell_source(cell)) for cell in parsed_cells]
```

    [('markdown', '## Demo'), ('code', 'value = 42')]

## Read a notebook

[`context`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/read.html#context) returns stable cell addresses and a compact representation. Start with a summary before asking for a whole chapter. The same result is useful for navigation and for assertions about the selection:

``` python
notebook_context = context("nbs/14_pyskill.ipynb", view="summary", verbose=False)
assert notebook_context["selection"]["matches"]
notebook_context
```

## Load the Pyskill

Install `nbskill` in the Python environment used by the agent (`pip install nbskill`, or `pip install -e .` for this checkout). The package registers `nbskill.skill` in the `pyskills` entry-point group. Discovery lists its scope without importing every problem area. Inspect the module and then the selected operation:

``` python
assert "nbskill.skill" in list_pyskills()
doc(skill.context)
```

    def context(
        target:str='project', scope:str='.', targets:list[str] | None=None, mode:str='auto', around:int=0,
        view:str | None=None, query:NoneType=None, include_re:str | None=None, exclude_re:str | None=None,
        max_matches:int=50, max_chars_per_cell:int=1200, context_lines:int=0, chapter:str | None=None,
        cell_type:str | None=None, include_output:bool=False, line_numbers:bool=False, verbose:bool=True
    ):"""Read one notebook-aware target, optionally narrowed by notebook filters."""

## Use with aai-coding

`aai-coding` owns the persistent session and ordinary Python files. `nbskill.skill` owns notebook source, generated modules, focused execution, and notebook review. [`generated_owner`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/foundation.html#generated_owner) chooses the route for each Python file; a repository marker alone does not make every file generated.

`install_nbskill --target codex` installs the local notebook routing skill. The Python Pyskill works independently of that host-specific installation.

## Search before implementing

[`reference_query`](https://MorsCerta-crypto.github.io/nbskill/knowledge.html#reference_query) searches local implementation references before a nontrivial helper is written. The knowledge notebook explains ingestion, dependency filters, and evidence. Query results depend on the local index and can load an embedding model, so the basic read/edit workflow does not require that optional path.

Problem memories store a problem, a verified solution, and tags for later reuse. Search them before choosing an approach; record new lessons after verification.

## Trace notebook relationships

The local graph links notebooks, cells, headings, symbols, and imports. Definition and call evidence helps a maintainer find related source before changing a symbol. Similarity edges are hints rather than runtime dependency guarantees. This example displays a small summary of the real source tree. Run it manually because building the graph scans all source notebooks:

``` python
graph = notebook_knowledge_graph_data("nbs")
dict(nodes=len(graph["nodes"]), edges=len(graph["edges"]), node_types=sorted({node["type"] for node in graph["nodes"]}), edge_types=sorted({edge["type"] for edge in graph["edges"]}))
```
